timescale_condensation.interpretation: finite-window condensed response changes with T although physical storage coefficients do not

bounded_conclusions: Hydrological memory makes forcing order physically observable when internal and forcing timescales interact.
Order dependence is not a universal monotone function of slowness. In the tested linear family it vanishes toward both extreme-slow and extreme-fast limits for different reasons.
A scalar affine response remains exact for each declared constant-H_c linear window, but its finite-window coefficient is window dependent.

The coupler need not know W_r and h_l individually to solve one such window if it receives an exact response tied to the committed origin. It does need enough temporal resolution or response information to represent a materially varying H_c trajectory.
A single average interface head cannot generally encode within-window boundary history.

The simple one-state physical limit is recovered under fast root-to-lower equilibration, but equality of physical limiting structure does not imply equality of continuous-time and implicit-Euler condensed coefficients.
nonclaims: no claim that the selected intermediate conductance scale is the global maximum of order sensitivity
no claim that production SWAP response is affine
no production u/q_u identity or admission
no claim that production coupling may ignore within-window head variation without an error qualification
